newsitem.title: INDIA: India PM given more time before confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: India PM given more time before confidence vote.

text.p: India's Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who was earlier on Monday asked by President Shankar Dayal Sharma to face a confidence vote in parliament by April 7, has been given four more days, a presidential communique said.

"The Prime Minister...called on the President late this evening and requested the President to allow time till Friday, 11th April, 1997 instead of Monday, 7th April, 1997 to seek a vote of confidence in the Lok Sabha (the lower house of parliament)..." the communique said.

It said Deve Gowda had cited a meeting of the Non-Aligned Movement's foreign ministers, scheduled to take place in New Delhi on April 7 and 8, and a Hindu new year's festival on April 8 and 9, as reasons for seeking the delay.
"The President has been pleased to permit the request," the communique said.

Deve Gowda's ten-month-old minority government was plunged into crisis on Sunday when its key ally, the Congress party, withdrew its support. Congress has also staked its claim to form a new government.
